literal: Distress to us to remain behind, he who went to a far distance thinking of, fragrant flowers felt ashamed, the eyes.
translation: Thinking of him who went far away, leaving me with nothing but distress, my eyes have wept so much that they now shrink in shame before fragrant flowers.
modern: நமக்குத் துன்பத்தை விட்டுவிட்டுத் தொலைதூரத்திற்குச் சென்ற காதலரை நினைத்து வருந்துவதால், என் கண்கள் அழகு கெட்டு நறுமணமுள்ள மலர்களுக்கு அஞ்சி நாணமடைகின்றன.
explanation: This couplet describes the physical toll of separation on the heroine's eyes. Her lover has departed to a distant land ('சேண் சென்றார்'), leaving her behind in deep distress ('சிறுமை நமக்கு ஒழிய'). By constantly thinking of him and weeping ('உள்ளி'), her eyes have lost their natural luster, becoming red and swollen. Previously, her beautiful eyes were compared to fresh, fragrant flowers ('நறுமலர்') and outshone them; now, having lost their beauty, the eyes feel ashamed ('நாணின') to even look at those flowers.
